questions.question: Are the market prices this lab measures against official NFL values?
questions.known: No. The archive's closing spread/total/moneyline come from the nflverse nfldata repository. The official NFL schedule pages carry no betting prices at all.
questions.unknown: Which sportsbook or consensus produced each price, and the exact minute each was captured.
questions.missingInfo: A price-level provenance field (book, capture timestamp) that the archive does not carry.
questions.wouldChange: Whether any ROI figure can be called an 'official' price comparison. Today it cannot.
questions.discovery: Re-check nfl.com schedule payloads for price keys (done: none) and, if a licensed price feed is purchased, re-run the backtest against it.
questions.answer: No — prices are non-official and are labelled NOT OFFICIAL on every page.

questions.question: Does the results/schedule mirror agree with the league's own published numbers?
questions.known: Yes, at the aggregate level. All 32 clubs' 2026 records and points for/against match nfl.com/standings exactly, and both recent Super Bowl results match their official game pages.
questions.unknown: Player-level 2026 totals: the reachable mirror has no 2026 week-level player file.
questions.missingInfo: A reachable 2026 player-week file, or an official per-player API.
questions.wouldChange: Whether prop research could start. Without it, props stay blocked.
questions.discovery: Retry the nflverse release asset from a network that permits release-assets host, or scrape the official player game logs.
questions.answer: Results and standings: 32/32 clubs agree. Player-level 2026: not verified.

questions.question: Who owns the market-price data, and may it be redistributed?
questions.known: The nflverse-data repository declares CC-BY-4.0. The nfldata repository from which the prices were read has no licence file in the tree at the commit used.
questions.unknown: Whether the underlying price vendor permits redistribution of derived prices.
questions.missingInfo: A written licence or permission covering derivative odds data.
questions.wouldChange: Whether this site may publish price-derived figures at all.
questions.discovery: Ask the nfldata maintainer for the provenance and licence of data/closing_lines.csv; until answered, keep derived prices off the public pages and show model-vs-market gaps only.

questions.question: Can GitHub release binaries be used directly, instead of a third-party mirror?
questions.known: No. This environment can reach github.com and api.github.com but not the release asset CDN (release-assets.githubusercontent.com).
questions.unknown: Whether the restriction is environmental or global.
questions.missingInfo: A CI runner (GitHub Actions) can reach the CDN; a local run cannot.
questions.wouldChange: Which files are first-party rather than mirrored.
questions.discovery: Run the same fetch in GitHub Actions and compare checksums with the mirror copy.
questions.answer: Release CDN is unreachable here; mirror used and labelled. CI can do better.

questions.question: What does 'originating my own line' mean here, precisely?
questions.known: A fair line is produced for every 2026 Week 11 game that has a market number: fair spread, fair total, fair moneyline and the break-even price.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner wants a pre-market number (before books post) or a comparison number (after books post).
questions.missingInfo: The intended use: deciding what to bet, or grading price accuracy.
questions.wouldChange: The timing of the model snapshot and which error metric matters.
questions.discovery: Read the Week 11 card; if the number arrives after the market, it is a comparison, not an origination.
questions.answer: Both numbers are published side by side so the distinction is visible.

questions.question: Is the fair-line model better than the closing market?
questions.known: No. On 7,413 graded games the model's mean absolute margin error is 10.52 points; the closing number's is 10.48. The de-vigged closing moneyline outscores the ratings everywhere.
questions.unknown: Whether a richer model (injuries, rest, weather, travel) closes that gap.
questions.missingInfo: Those inputs are not in the archive.
questions.wouldChange: Whether any line can be published as an alternative to the market rather than a transparent benchmark.
questions.discovery: Add one input at a time and require it to beat the current model on identical games.
questions.answer: No — the market is better, and the site says so.

questions.question: How much of the fair line is a fixed constant rather than a model?
questions.known: The probability-to-margin mapping is an OLS fit: intercept 0.34 points, slope 31.71 points per probability unit, fitted on 7,413 graded games. The league mean total is 44.29.
questions.unknown: How stable those constants are out of sample.
questions.missingInfo: A stability check across disjoint seasons.
questions.wouldChange: Confidence in the fair spread for extreme probabilities.
questions.discovery: Refit the mapping within each season and compare the coefficients.
questions.answer: The mapping is explicit and printed on the page; nothing is hidden in a black box.

questions.question: Are the market numbers for an unplayed week final?
questions.known: 2026 Week 11 carries 13 games with prices in the archive, captured 2026-11-13.
questions.unknown: Whether those are closing or current-in-progress prices.
questions.missingInfo: A capture timestamp per price.
questions.wouldChange: Whether the gap between the model and the number is exploitable or already closed.
questions.discovery: Snapshot the same games again later and diff.

questions.question: Has any strategy demonstrated skill rather than luck?
questions.known: No. 8 strategies were tested on 300-5,000 graded bets each. None has a week-block bootstrap interval entirely above zero. The best point estimate (+0.4%) has an interval of -2.7% to +4.0%.
questions.unknown: Whether a better-specified model would.
questions.missingInfo: Better inputs, which are blocked (see Q10, Q11).
questions.wouldChange: Nothing is reward-eligible until one strategy passes every gate.
questions.discovery: Only a frozen prospective trial can promote a strategy (gate G7).
questions.answer: No. Zero of 8 tested strategies earned a rank above 'unproven'.

questions.question: What is the pre-declared evidence bar for a strategy to be considered skilful?
questions.known: Minimum 300 graded bets; a bootstrap interval that excludes zero ROI; a p-value corrected for the family of 8 tested strategies; and a frozen prospective trial.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner accepts these thresholds.
questions.missingInfo: A decision on thresholds, which is a policy choice, not a fact.
questions.wouldChange: How many strategies appear on the leaderboard and which can earn rewards.
questions.discovery: Choose the thresholds on the Suggestions page; the engine will re-label automatically.

questions.question: Are player-prop and same-game-parlay strategies testable with what we have?
questions.known: No. There are no prop prices of any kind, and parlay prices are the product of two leg prices, which is not how a book prices a correlated parlay.
questions.unknown: Whether the same-game parlay prices any book quoted historically can be obtained.
questions.missingInfo: A timestamped prop and SGP price archive.
questions.wouldChange: Whether prop and combo strategies move from BLOCKED to TESTED.
questions.discovery: Buy or licence a price archive; log it with a capture timestamp per quote.
questions.answer: Blocked. Declared, scored as zero evidence, and shown as BLOCKED — not hidden.

questions.question: Does a parlay's quoted payout reflect its true joint probability?
questions.known: The archive has no SGP prices, so the two- and three-leg parlays were priced at the product of the leg decimals, which is an upper bound on what a book pays for correlated legs.
questions.unknown: The real SGP hold and correlation adjustment for the legs used.
questions.missingInfo: Book-specific SGP pricing rules.
questions.wouldChange: The measured parlay ROI, which is currently the only positive point estimate (+10%) and still statistically indistinguishable from zero.
questions.discovery: Collect actual SGP quotes for the same legs and re-price.

questions.question: How correlated are the markets and players we would combine?
questions.known: Measured: spread-cover vs over phi = +0.014 (n=7,109); moneyline vs over phi = +0.005 (n=5,220); QB passing yards vs his WR1 receiving yards phi = +0.29 (n=307); RB1 vs RB2 rushing phi = +0.07 (n=311); WR1 vs WR2 receiving phi = +0.003 (n=321).
questions.unknown: Whether those correlations hold in the 2026 player data.
questions.missingInfo: A 2026 player-week file.
questions.wouldChange: How much a parlay's fair price moves away from the independent product.
questions.discovery: Recompute when the 2026 file is reachable; the script is parameterised by season.

questions.question: Should the leaderboard rank by ROI at all?
questions.known: Ranking by raw ROI rewards the highest-variance strategy. The three-leg parlay (n=384) shows +10.0% ROI with an interval from -30.9% to +57.3% — the widest on the board.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner prefers risk-adjusted rank or evidence-weighted rank.
questions.missingInfo: A scoring-policy decision.
questions.wouldChange: The order of the leaderboard.
questions.discovery: Pick a policy on the Suggestions page; the default here ranks by the lower bound of the ROI interval.

questions.question: What would reward a strategy, and what stops a lucky winner?
questions.known: No strategy is reward-eligible. Eligibility requires passing all 8 gates including a frozen prospective trial and a human release review.
questions.unknown: The actual reward mechanism, and whether real money is involved (legal review needed).
questions.missingInfo: Owner decision plus legal review.
questions.wouldChange: Whether the leaderboard can pay anything at all.
questions.discovery: Paper-only first; record predictions before outcomes for a fixed horizon.

questions.question: Can official 1st/2nd/3rd/4th-string depth order be obtained from the NFL?
questions.known: Not from this environment: nfl.com/teams/<club>/depth-chart returns HTTP 404. The roster page returns 200 but lists position and ACT status only, with no order.
questions.unknown: Whether a depth chart exists behind a different official URL or an official API.
questions.missingInfo: A confirmed official depth-order source.
questions.wouldChange: Whether the tier column is read from the league or computed by this lab.
questions.discovery: Probe nfl.com team sub-pages and the NFL's public data endpoints from CI.
questions.answer: Not retrieved. Tiers are therefore computed from production and labelled as such.

questions.question: Which players are actually unavailable this week, and at what tier?
questions.known: For three 2026 Week 10 games: 65 officially listed players, 8 Out, 1 Questionable, 56 with a blank game status. A production-based tier is attached to each.
questions.unknown: The other Week 10 games and all of Week 11.
questions.missingInfo: Transcription of the remaining official injury pages (or a parser for them).
questions.wouldChange: The coverage of the tracker page.
questions.discovery: Extend the capture to every game of the week; the page is keyed by season and week.

questions.question: How many points is a missing tier-1 player worth?
questions.known: Measured on 414 club-weeks of 2025: tier-1 offence out -> own points 22.01 vs 22.98 (-0.97, interval -3.22 to +1.38). Tier-1 defence out -> points allowed 23.42 vs 22.62 (+0.80, interval -1.58 to +3.14). Quarterback alone: -4.99 points over 18 club-weeks, too small a sample to interval.
questions.unknown: Whether the effect is causal, and how it scales with tier 2/3/4.
questions.missingInfo: Multiple seasons with practice status and snap counts.
questions.wouldChange: Whether injury adjustment can be a betting input at all.
questions.discovery: Repeat across 2016-2025 once the full injury files are reachable; require stability.
questions.answer: No measurable effect found beyond the quarterback point estimate, whose sample is too small.

questions.question: Does a backup replacing a starter show up in the score at all?
questions.known: Only weakly. Position-group differences are all inside their intervals except the small-sample groups, which cannot be interval-estimated.
questions.unknown: Whether an individual-level (not group-level) replacement effect exists.
questions.missingInfo: Snap counts and participation data, absent here.
questions.wouldChange: Whether a 'backup tier' feature would add information.
questions.discovery: Join snap counts when reachable; measure the drop when the tier-1 player's snap share is replaced.

questions.question: Is the official injury report's blank status meaningful?
questions.known: The page leaves Practice Status and Game Status blank for most listed players; 56 of 65 rows in the captured games are blank in at least one field.
questions.unknown: Whether blank means 'no game designation' or 'not yet published'.
questions.missingInfo: The league's documentation of the report format.
questions.wouldChange: Whether a blank should be treated as available.
questions.discovery: Compare the same report across practice days to see blanks fill in.

questions.question: Is the luck test correct when bet prices differ?
questions.known: An earlier pooled break-even win-rate test was wrong for mixed prices: it compared win counts while the money depends on the price. It has been replaced by a per-bet null using the de-vigged closing market probability of the side taken, with 10,000 seeded simulations.
questions.unknown: Nothing further — the defect was identified, corrected and recorded on the Method page.
questions.missingInfo: None.
questions.wouldChange: The three-leg parlay's significance fell from p = 0.0005 to p = 0.218. No other strategy crosses the significance line.
questions.discovery: Re-run the engine; the seed is fixed so the result is reproducible.
questions.answer: Yes now, no before. The old figure was withdrawn, not hidden.

questions.question: Where do suggestions get reviewed before anything is built?
questions.known: This lab adds a dedicated Suggestions page with a decision column and a recommended path.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner wants a voting or scoring mechanism.
questions.missingInfo: Owner preference.
questions.wouldChange: Whether suggestions are ranked by the owner or by the lab.
questions.discovery: Open the Suggestions page; each row names the decision required.
questions.answer: Published, with cost/risk/reversibility and a recommendation per item.

questions.question: How can a reader tell an official value from a model value at a glance?
questions.known: Every row carries a source link and an OFFICIAL / MIRROR / MODEL / NOT OFFICIAL label.
questions.unknown: Whether the labelling is legible enough in practice.
questions.missingInfo: Owner feedback after review.
questions.wouldChange: The badge design, not the data.
questions.discovery: Review the Flagged page and the source badges on any table.

note: ANSWERED items carry the answer. UNVERIFIED and AWAITING-DECISION items are the open decisions; each names the exact discovery step that would settle it.
